Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruit
Avoid working in field when plants are wet

symptoms: Severe upward curling and yellowing of leaves, stunted growth, flower drop, very low yield
cause: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus — transmitted by whitefly
treatment: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL at 0.5ml per litre to control whitefly
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Install yellow sticky traps at 10 per acre to monitor whitefly
prevention: Use virus-resistant varieties like Arka Samrat, use silver mulch to repel whitefly

symptoms: Small circular spots with dark brown border and grey centre on lower leaves, tiny black dots in spot centre
treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2g per litre every 10 days
Remove infected lower leaves and destroy
Avoid overhead irrigation and splashing soil onto leaves
prevention: Crop rotation, remove crop debris after harvest, stake plants to improve airflow

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, yellowing of surrounding tissue, premature defoliation
treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP at 2g per litre every 7 days

Remove infected leaves and avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers, practice 3-year crop rotation

prevention: Plant resistant varieties like Kufri Bahar, avoid excessive irrigation

symptoms: Small golden to brick-red oval pustules on both leaf surfaces, powdery spore masses, severe cases cause leaf death
treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC at 1ml per litre at early stage

Remove severely infected plants to reduce spread
prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrid varieties, early planting before rust season

Ensure good drainage and avoid dense planting
prevention: Use resistant hybrid varieties, crop rotation with non-host crops

prevention: Use disease-free certified seeds, avoid working in wet conditions

Apply Captan 50% WP at 2g per litre post-flowering

prevention: Remove all infected debris before new season, maintain open canopy

Apply Copper Oxychloride 50% WP at 3g per litre
Remove old infected leaves and avoid wetting foliage
prevention: Plant disease-resistant varieties, use raised beds for good drainage

symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves, leaf distortion and curling, stunted plant growth, reduced fruit quality
cause: Tomato Mosaic Virus — transmitted by contact and insects

Disinfect tools with 1% sodium hypochlorite between plants
prevention: Use virus-free certified seeds, wash hands before handling plants, control aphids early
